diagnosis.hypothesis: Failing pairs were external1→web1 and web1→external1. Inspection of fw-ext's firewall config (PB-19 pattern) showed a stray rule 1 { action drop } named 'ibn-shadow-deny' in the DMZ-TO-OUTSIDE ruleset with no match conditions, shadowing rules 10 (return-traffic) and 20 (web1-ping-outside). Removed that single rule via `delete firewall ipv4 name DMZ-TO-OUTSIDE rule 1`; default-action drop and all other rulesets/zones were left untouched. After the change, all 10 lab_connectivity pairs pass with 0% loss, including the previously-failing external1↔web1 path.
diagnosis.reference: On the firewall fw-ext, a deny rule was placed ahead of the allow rules in ruleset DMZ-TO-OUTSIDE (DMZ to OUTSIDE), shadowing them so the traffic is dropped.

arguments.name: DMZ-TO-OUTSIDE
arguments.reason: Rule 1 'ibn-shadow-deny' (action drop, no match conditions) sits before rule 10 (return-traffic) and rule 20 (web1-ping-outside), shadowing them and dropping all DMZ->OUTSIDE traffic. Removing it restores the intended web1->external1 ping path without loosening segmentation (default-action drop stays, and the remaining accept rules are specific).

final_response.summary: Failing pairs were external1→web1 and web1→external1. Inspection of fw-ext's firewall config (PB-19 pattern) showed a stray rule 1 { action drop } named 'ibn-shadow-deny' in the DMZ-TO-OUTSIDE ruleset with no match conditions, shadowing rules 10 (return-traffic) and 20 (web1-ping-outside). Removed that single rule via `delete firewall ipv4 name DMZ-TO-OUTSIDE rule 1`; default-action drop and all other rulesets/zones were left untouched. After the change, all 10 lab_connectivity pairs pass with 0% loss, including the previously-failing external1↔web1 path.
